text: A linked list is a linear data structure, in which the elements are not stored at contiguous memory locations. The elements in a linked list are linked using pointers.
A linked list consists of nodes where each node contains a data field and a reference(link) to the next node in the list. class Node { int data; Node next; }
To insert a node at the beginning, time complexity is O(1). To insert at the end, it takes O(N). Insertion is faster than arrays because no shifting is required.
